title: Interaction bundles — seedpad for compact feature PRD
content:
Context:
- Observation: many products implement the same short multi-turn sequences (e.g., clarify intent -> capture slot set -> ack) and each call to the LLM is expensive (latency + token cost).
- Idea: define "interaction bundles" — compact, pre-authorable microflows that represent common multi-turn interactions and can be invoked as a single logical operation by the client. Backend maps that to optimized execution (cached prefixes, condensed prompts, optional local heuristics).

Goals (high level):
1) Reduce per-conversation token spend for repeated short flows by 20–50% for target workloads.
2) Reduce tail latency for common microflows by enabling a single RPC with server-side microflow orchestration and caching.
3) Provide a simple authoring model so product teams can create bundles without deep prompt-engineering.
4) Support gradual migration: fallback to plain prompts for bundles not available.

Who benefits:
- Small assistants and chatbots with lots of structured short exchanges (forms, clarifying questions, settings wizards).
- Platform teams wanting predictable unit economics for common journeys.

Core concepts (rough):
- Bundle: named artifact that encapsulates an ordered microflow of steps (messages + checks + optional tool calls).
- Variant: model/tuning/quantization profile attached to a bundle for cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Invocation API: clients call bundles by name with minimal context and receive a compact, structured response.
- Execution engine heuristics: server can short-circuit steps if stable state in KV cache, or replace heavy model steps with heuristic logic (e.g., regex extraction) when confidence high.

Proposed API sketch (pseudo):
- POST /v1/bundles/run
  body: { bundle_id: "slot-capture-v1", context: {user_text: "I want to book"}, mode: "latency|economy|full", session_id: "s-123" }
  response: { status: "ok", steps: [{name: "clarify", text: "Which date?", tokens_used: 48}, {name: "capture", slots: {date: "2025-05-12"}}], meta: {model: "rwi-tiny-v1", cost_tokens: 112, fallback: false} }

User stories (examples):
- As a product engineer, I want to call a named microflow so I don't manually orchestrate clarifying turns in the client.
- As an SRE, I want unit-level telemetry for bundles (p50/p95 latency, tokens, cache-hit rate) so we can track economics.
- As a privacy officer, I want the ability to pin bundles to Private deployment only and enforce no-storage policy.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Authoring UI/manifest: write a simple YAML/JSON that defines up to 6 steps with templated prompts + output mappings.
- Server-side runtime: accept bundle run API and execute steps with continuous batching and KV-prefix caching support.
- Fallback behavior: if bundle not found, return 404 or allow pass-through to regular completion API.
- Telemetry: emit per-invocation metrics (tokens, latency, cache-hit).
- Tests: end-to-end flow for slot-capture and simple confirmation microflow.

Data model sketch (manifest):
- id: string
- description: string
- steps: list of { name, prompt_template, output_schema, optional, max_tokens }
- variants: list of { id, model_hint, quant_profile }
- constraints: { privacy: allow_persist, allowed_deployments }

Open questions / risks:
- Authoring complexity: how to make step templates accessible to PMs non-engineers? Need simple UI + preview.
- Model divergence: bundles authored with one model might produce different behaviors on another variant. Need regression tests per variant.
- Billing semantics: charge per invocation vs per-token? If server-side short-circuits, user expectations on cost must match billing.
- Storage: shrinking token spend via cache may require storing prefixes — privacy implications. Provide opt-out.
- ATO/enterprise concerns if bundles can call external tools or webhooks.

Experiment plan (phases):
Phase 0 (internal hack): implement runtime shim that sequences 2–3 completions using existing completion API and records tokens. Run with 3 internal bundles.
Phase 1 (canary): expose bundles via API behind feature flag. Run with 2 customers (low-risk) and measure cost + latency.
Phase 2 (productize): authoring UI + variants + rollout controls in Console.

Metrics to track:
- Cost per logical interaction (tokens + compute) vs baseline. Target: -30% token cost on median for short flows.
- P50/P95 latency for bundle invocation. Target: p95 < 350ms for optimized variants.
- Cache hit rate and % of steps short-circuited.
- Bundle adoption rate (#teams using, #invocations/day).

Operational considerations:
- Deployment modes: Hosted: bundles stored & executed by Redwood. Dedicated/Private: bundles may be customer-managed; provide export/import model.
- Versioning: manifest versions with rollout flags; support canary percent.
- Rollback: if quality regressions detected, automatically revert variant to more capable model.

UX / authoring notes (brainstorm):
- Minimal editor: step list + preview pane that shows simulated conversation with token counts.
- Allow designers to attach small JSON schemas for step outputs so clients get structured payloads.
- Provide built-in slot extraction helpers (date, email, enum) that generate light-weight heuristics rather than always relying on LLM.
- Marketplace idea: shareable bundle templates (form-wizard, feedback-collector). Possibly curated by Redwood.

Example manifest (rough):
---
 id: "meeting-scheduler-compact-v1"
 description: "Ask for date and time, then confirm and produce structured event payload"
 steps:
   - name: "clarify_date"
     prompt_template: "User said: {{user_text}}. Ask: What date works?"
     output_schema: {date: "iso"}
   - name: "clarify_time"
     prompt_template: "User: {{last_user}}. Ask: What time?"
     output_schema: {time: "hh:mm"}
 variants:
   - id: "latency-optim"
     model_hint: "rwi-tiny-v1"
     quant_profile: "int4"

Implementation notes for runtime team (quick):
- Reuse existing KV cache for prefix reuse; add bundle namespace to keys.
- Allow step-level bypass to deterministic extractor functions.
- Instrument token accounting per-step; expose in telemetry.
- API surface should be backward-compatible: allow a passthrough mode where bundle invocation simply expands to a sequence of existing completions for debugging.

Next actions (to myself):
- Align with Lina Morales on privacy constraints (email).
- Spike: server shim PoC call sequence (2 days).
- Draft Confluence page with high-level diagrams and sample telemetry (JIRA-2145).
- Schedule 30m sync with Maya + Kai to prioritize initial bundle templates.

Notes to self (scratch):
- Keep scope tiny for MVP: 2 canonical bundles (slot-capture, quick-confirm).
- Don't over-automate authoring in first pass; simpler manifest wins.
- Consider billing note: bill per-token but show estimated cost per invocation in Console.

Unresolved UX decisions:
- Should clients be able to inspect intermediate prompts? (security + privacy)
- How to represent partial success when a step fails? standardized error schema?

End of seedpad.
